source.title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Revisited

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Classify all finite-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean space E^{n+1}; in particular, classify all finite-type surfaces in E^3.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Classify all finite type hypersurfaces in En+1. In particular, classify all finite type surfaces in E3.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Is every compact finite-type surface in Euclidean 3-space E^3 a sphere?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. The only compact finite type surfaces in E3 are the spheres.
However, Conjecture 1 remains open.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Are hyperspheres the only compact hypersurfaces of finite type in Euclidean space?

evidence.quote: It also seems to the author that hyperspheres are the only compact hypersurfaces of finite type in Euclidean space.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Classify finite-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere embedded in Euclidean space E^{n+2}.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Classify finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in En+2.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For surfaces in the standard 3-sphere S^3 embedded in E^4, are the only finite-type surfaces the minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres, and products of plane circles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. Minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres and products of plane circles are the only finite type surfaces in S3 (imbedded standardly in E4).
Remark 1. This conjecture stays open.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere embedded in E^{n+2}; in particular, classify the 3-dimensional 2-type hypersurfaces of S^4 embedded in E^5.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of En+2. In particular, classify 3-dimensional 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere S4 in E5.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a Dupin hypersurface M of a hypersphere, characterize when M is of finite type, and determine when a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere is isoparametric.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. When is a Dupin hypersurface M of a hypersphere of finite type? When is a finite type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere isoparametric?

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a finite-type submanifold contained in a hypersphere, call it mass-symmetric when the constant vector c in the spectral decomposition is the center of that hypersphere. Do there exist 2-type surfaces in S^4 that are not mass-symmetric?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Do there exist (non-mass-symmetric) 2-type surfaces in S4?

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Is every n-dimensional non-null 2-type submanifold of E^{n+2} with constant mean curvature spherical, meaning contained in a hypersphere?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Is every n-dimensional non-null 2-type submanifold of En+2 with constant mean curvature spherical?

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a finite-type submanifold contained in a hypersphere, call it mass-symmetric when the constant vector c in the spectral decomposition is the center of that hypersphere. Do there exist 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere of a Euclidean space; in particular, do there exist mass-symmetric 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Do there exist 2-type surfaces which lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere of a Euclidean space? In particular, do there exist mass-symmetric 2-type surfaces which lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere?

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a k-type immersion x with spectral pieces x_i, let E_i be the linear span of the vectors x_i(p) as p varies over M. Call x linearly independent when the subspaces E_1, ..., E_k are linearly independent. Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Study and classify linearly independent 2-type immersions.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a k-type immersion x with spectral pieces x_i, let E_i be the linear span of the vectors x_i(p) as p varies over M. Call x linearly independent when the subspaces E_1, ..., E_k are linearly independent. Study and classify linearly independent submanifolds of codimension 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Study and classify linearly independent submanifolds of codimension 2.

accepted.question_text: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. Are all biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces minimal, equivalently are there any nonminimal biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean space?
accepted.context_brief: Chen biharmonic conjecture in Euclidean space

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Other than minimal submanifolds of Em, which submanifolds of Em are biharmonic?
Conjecture 3: The only biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces are the minimal ones.
Remark 2. Conjecture 3 remains open.

accepted.question_text: For a biharmonic submanifold of a Riemannian manifold whose sectional curvature is non-positive, must the submanifold be minimal?

evidence.quote: Every biharmonic submanifold of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive sectional curvature is minimal.
On the other hand, it was proved by Y.-L. Ou and L. Tang in [OuT] that the generalized Chen’s biharmonic conjecture is false in general.

accepted.question_text: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. For hypersurfaces of Euclidean spaces, is every biharmonic hypersurface minimal?

evidence.quote: Biharmonic Conjecture for Hypersurfaces: Every biharmonic hypersurface of Euclidean spaces is minimal.

accepted.question_text: For an isometric immersion x: M -> E^m with mean curvature vector H, call the immersion biharmonic when Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0; minimal immersions are biharmonic. For complete submanifolds of Euclidean space, is every complete biharmonic submanifold minimal?

evidence.quote: Global Version of Chen’s biharmonic Conjecture: Every complete biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space is minimal.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Does every null 2-type surface in Euclidean 4-space have constant mean curvature?

evidence.quote: The author doesn’t know whether every null 2-type surface in a Euclidean 4-space has constant mean curvature.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds; in particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.

accepted.question_text: Call an immersion x: M -> E^m finite type when its position vector can be written as x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is constant and each nonconstant component x_i is a Laplacian eigenfunction, Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. If the eigenvalues lambda_i are mutually distinct, call the immersion k-type; if one eigenvalue is zero, call it null k-type. For a compact homogeneous manifold N with irreducible isotropy action, the i-th standard immersion is built from an orthonormal basis of the eigenspace for the i-th positive Laplacian eigenvalue; the first standard immersion uses the first positive eigenvalue. Let N be an irreducible compact homogeneous manifold immersed in a Euclidean space E^N by its first standard immersion phi, and let M be a submanifold of N. Characterize when M is finite type in E^N via phi; in particular, characterize when M is 1-type or 2-type in E^N via phi.
accepted.context_brief: Finite type under first standard immersions

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let N be an irreducible compact homogeneous manifold immersed in a Euclidean space EN by its first standard immersion phi and M a submanifold of N. When M is of finite type in EN via phi? In particular, when M is of 1- or 2-type in EN via phi?
